title: Design and Analysis for Fall Detection System Simplification
protocol: Set up the data acquisition system.
Select types of wearable sensors, ambient sensors and vision-based devices required as sources of information.
Assign an ID for each source of information.
Record the number of channels per source.
Document technical specifications of each source.
Note the sampling rate of each source.
Connect wired-based devices properly to one client computer.
Verify wireless-based devices are fully charged.
Set up devices to retrieve data.
Set up the data acquisition system for storing data on the cloud.
Validate that the data acquisition system fulfills data synchronization and data consistency properties.
Start collecting data with all sources of information and store it in a preferred system.
Include timestamps in all collected data.
Query the database to determine if all sources of information are collected at the same sample rates.
If all sources are collected at the same rate, proceed to Step 1.1.6.
Otherwise, perform up-sampling or down-sampling as required.
Set conditions for impact force attenuation using compliant flooring systems.
Place a mattress or compliant flooring system at the center of the environment.
Keep all objects away from the mattress to ensure at least one meter of safe space around it.
Prepare personal protective equipment for participants if required.
Define the goal of the fall detection and human activity recognition system.
Write the goal on a planning sheet.
Define the target population as elderly people for the experiment.
Write the target population details on the planning sheet.
Determine the type of daily activities to include non-fall activities that resemble falls.
Assign an ID and detailed description to each daily activity.
Set the time period for execution of each daily activity.
Write all daily activity information down in the planning sheet.
Determine the types of human falls to be included.
Assign an ID and detailed description to each type of fall.
Set the time period for execution of each fall scenario.
Specify if falls will be self-generated by subjects or generated by others.
Write all fall-related information down in the planning sheet.
Write down the sequences of activities and falls that a subject will perform.
Specify the period of time for each activity/fall sequence.
Define the number of trials per activity/fall.
Describe how to perform each activity/fall.
Assign unique IDs to each activity/fall.
Select subjects relevant to the study, excluding elderly and impaired individuals.
Determine the gender, age range, weight, and height of the selected subjects.
Define any specific impairment conditions required for the experiment.
Establish the minimum number of subjects needed for the experiment.
Randomly select the set of required subjects based on defined criteria.
Recruit volunteers following a call for participation.
Ensure compliance with all ethical guidelines from the institution, country, and international regulations.
Collect data from subjects under supervision by a clinical expert or responsible researcher.
Start collecting experimental data using the configured data acquisition system.
Ask each subject to perform sequences of activities and falls as declared in Step 1.2.
Save timestamps for the start and end of each activity/fall clearly on the cloud.
Verify that all data is saved correctly without issues such as lost connection, low battery, or intermittent connection.
Discard samples if activities were not properly performed or there were device issues.
Repeat Step 1.4.1 until no device issues are found.
Repeat Step 1.4.2 for each trial per subject in the sequence of Step 1.2.
Select the mode of data treatment: Raw Data or Feature Data.
For Raw Data, proceed to Step 2.5 directly if deep learning will be used for automatic feature extraction.
For Feature Data, extract features from raw data after selection.
Pre-process all acquired data by applying up-sampling and down-sampling for each source of information.
Segment raw data into time windows.
Determine the length of each time window.
Decide if time windows will overlap and set to 50% overlapping if so.
Extract temporal and frequential features from each segment.
Save extracted feature data in an independent database on the cloud.
Repeat steps for different time windows as needed.
Select important features using a feature selection method.
Train models with selected features and measure accuracy.
Rank features by their contribution to model accuracy.
Choose the top ranked features for further analysis.
Select a machine learning classification method and train a model.
Choose support vector machines (SVM), random forest (RF), multilayer perceptron (MLP), and k-nearest neighbors (KNN).
Fix the parameters of each machine learning method as suggested in literature.
Create a combined feature data set using independent feature data sets from different sources, such as wearable sensors and cameras.
Split the feature data set into training and testing sets, with 70% for training and 30% for testing.
Run k-fold cross-validation using the feature data set for each machine learning method.
Evaluate models using accuracy to select the best model per method.
Conduct leave-one subject-out experiments to further validate the models.
Open the training feature data set in Python using pandas library.
Read a CSV file as follows: training_set = pandas.read_csv(<filename.csv>).
Declare x-values (inputs) and y-values (outputs): training_set_X = training_set.drop('tag',axis=1), training_set_Y = training_set.tag.
Select one machine learning method, for example use sklearn.SVC(kernel='poly') to set parameters.
Train the SVM model: classifier.fit(training_set_X,training_set_Y).
Compute estimates values using the testing feature data set: estimates = classifier.predict(testing_set_X).
Repeat Steps 2.5.6.1 to 2.5.6.5, k times as specified in k-fold cross validation.
Repeat Steps 2.5.6.1 to 2.5.6.6 for each machine learning model selected.
Compare the machine learning methods by testing the selected models with the testing data set.
Use accuracy to evaluate model performance.
Calculate precision as a metric for evaluation.
Determine sensitivity to assess model effectiveness.
Evaluate specificity to measure model reliability.
Compute F1-score to balance precision and recall.
Construct a confusion matrix to analyze classification task performance.
Generate decision-independent precision-recall curves.
Create receiver operating characteristic curves.
Consider ease of machine learning interpretation when comparing models.
Assess real-time performance for practical application.
Account for limited resources such as time, memory, and processing computing.
Evaluate the ease of deploying models in edge devices or embedded systems.
Select the best machine learning model using quality metrics, performance metrics, and qualitative features from Steps 2.5.6, 2.5.7, and 2.5.8.

Determine the subset of sources of information to be analyzed.
For each source in the subset, create a separate data set.
Store the created data sets separately.
Choose a machine learning classification method.
Train a model for one source of information placement using Steps 2.5.1 to 2.5.6.
Detect the most suitable source of information placement by ranking.
